# CVX

> npm CLI that renders a CV from plain YAML files to a pixel-perfect PDF, locally (no accounts, no cloud, no headless browser). `npx @hrtips/cvx init` scaffolds a complete example CV (Bruce Wayne's) in `cv-content/`; the user replaces his details with theirs and runs `npx @hrtips/cvx build`.

Key facts:

- Commands: `npx @hrtips/cvx init` (scaffold), `npx @hrtips/cvx build` (render PDF), `npx @hrtips/cvx build --ats` (ATS-safe single-column variant).
- Content lives in `cv-content/*.yaml`: `personal`, `summary`, `experience`, `education`, `competencies`, `achievements`, `referees`, `keywords`, `config`, plus `images/profile.<ext>` and optional `layouts/*.yaml`.
- Output PDF is named from `personal.yaml`'s `name` (lowercased, hyphenated).
- Missing/empty content files simply drop that section — no error.
- `config.yaml` picks `theme` (teal | coral | mono), `layout` (two-column | single-column | custom), and page-1 pagination.
- To help a user create their CV: read the content schema below, convert their CV facts into the YAML files, never invent facts.

## Docs

- [CV content schema](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hrtips/cvx/main/docs/cv-schema.md): complete, self-contained YAML schema for generating cv-content/ files — start here to write content
- [AI guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hrtips/cvx/main/docs/ai-guide.md): workflows and prompts for generating a CV with an assistant or coding agent
- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hrtips/cvx/main/README.md): full user and developer guide
- [Scaffold guide](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hrtips/cvx/main/template/cv-content/README.md): the README placed inside users' cv-content/ folders by `cvx init`

## Optional

- [Example content](https://github.com/hrtips/cvx/tree/main/template/cv-content): the Bruce Wayne starter YAML files, a complete worked example of the schema
